doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Black and white players, and the meaning of the band's name
summary: He sees deeper blues feeling in black players and explains the name Harlem Blues and Jazz Band.

bands.name: Chris Barber's Jazz and Blues Band

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Did you, or do you distinguish between white and black players?

In a way I do because there is a deeper blues feeling to the black players I feel. And that’s why I put “blues” first. Chris Barber’s band in England is Chris Barber’s Jazz and Blues band. Mine is the Harlem — because I wanted to honor Harlem’s contribution, everybody knows about Chicago, everybody knows about New Orleans, but Harlem I thought I might get a little bit of a mystique or a cachet from the name, and I wanted to honor Harlem so I said Harlam, and then I wanted “blues” to come first. In the beginning
it was a cumbersome name, the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band. But people are used to it now.
Yeah. A name becomes a good name if it has a good band. Eventually.
So there was a reason behind every word. Harlem, blues and jazz.
